ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Romans being conquered in the Quran?
ai.summary: This verse, revealed in Mecca around 615-616 CE, marks a pivotal moment in early Islamic history as it coincides with the Sassanid Persian victory over the Byzantines at Antioch. Shia and Sunni scholars alike view the subsequent Roman victory at the Battle of Issus (622 CE) as a miraculous fulfillment of divine prophecy, serving as a tangible sign (ayah) of God's sovereignty over worldly empires and a precursor to the spread of Islam.
